title: A dwarf galaxy ravaged by grand design
caption: The dwarf galaxy NGC 5474, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows NGC 5474, a dwarf galaxy in Ursa Major, some 21 million light-years from us. The word dwarf can mislead, since the galaxy holds several billion stars. It only seems small next to the Milky Way, which has hundreds of billions.

NGC 5474 belongs to the Messier 101 Group. The brightest member is the Pinwheel Galaxy, Messier 101, a well-known spiral whose clear, well-defined arms class it as a grand design galaxy, like Messier 81 and Messier 74.

Messier 101 has other neighbours in the group, and gravitational interactions with them may have helped give it its distinctive shape. In the same way, interactions with Messier 101 may explain the distortions seen in NGC 5474. Our own Local Group and the Messier 101 Group both lie within the Virgo Supercluster, which makes NGC 5474 a neighbour of ours in galactic terms.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using filters at 606 and 814 nm, in visible and near-infrared light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and Hubble resolves stars in this galaxy that no eye could pick out.
